title: Nonuniform-temperature global Arrhenius creep patch
purpose: Verify that a finite-element temperature field is evaluated at the shared creep quadrature identity and is consumed by the same backward-Euler update, analytical tangent, Newton path, output, and checkpoint identity as the global power-law creep state.
physics: three-dimensional small-strain Mises power-law creep with a prescribed nonuniform Arrhenius temperature field

execution.evidence: A unit-cube relaxation patch carries a linear 800--900 K temperature field. The accepted integration-point temperature range and nonuniform equivalent creep strain are retained in the structured result.

observables: TEMP is present as the finite-element field supplied to the constitutive step.
Every accepted increment records the minimum and maximum temperature evaluated at creep quadrature points.
The hotter and colder integration points develop different CEEQ under the same imposed displacement path.
The temperature description participates in checkpoint compatibility.
acceptance: All consumed temperatures are finite and positive kelvin values.
Quadrature extrema lie strictly inside the 800--900 K nodal range and preserve its symmetric mean.
The global step converges and the CEEQ field is nonuniform.
Temperature extrema are available both as quantities and accepted-increment histories.
limitations: The temperature field is prescribed for the creep solve; this benchmark does not transfer an evolving transient heat history.
Elastic and creep parameters other than the normalized Arrhenius coefficient remain temperature independent.
This is a regression and integration benchmark, not external component validation.
